Declared types in other verified sources are useful hypotheses, not proof of a shared historical header.

target_bytes_note: Raw target includes loader-chain words; use masked disassembly and semantic bindings for source inference

compiler_profile.note: Profile is attached to the object context; it is not a per-function switch and the grinder cannot change it

reconstruction_rules.rule: LINK 5.30 /FARCALLTRANSLATION rewrites a same-segment far call into NOP; PUSH CS; CALL near (five bytes). Write an ordinary far call to the named function; the strict matcher validates the linker transformation independently.

Declaration order can determine DS versus ES code generation: the compiler keeps the last-loaded far selector live, so the order in which far objects are first referenced in the source (not the extern declaration order) fixes ES reuse and the CONST selector-pool order. Reorder references, not declarations, to change selector traffic.

When the historical code holds a parameter's value in SI/DI throughout, an explicit local copy of the parameter (register variable candidate) can be required; the compiler does not enregister [bp+n] parameters directly.

Arrays are frequently word-indexed (SHL 1 / ADD reg,reg before the displacement). Preserve the observed element width: declare int arrays for two-byte strides, char arrays for byte strides, eight-byte structs for SHL 3.

Never invent a convenient symbol when MAPSYM provides the real one: use the exact name from direct_data_bindings; an unnamed operand inside a named public array is an index into that array, not a new private object.

A matching numeric offset does not establish object identity: equal offsets in different segments are different objects, and a BSS word placed by constraint inside another object's data proves nothing.

Far-object identity requires selector/segment evidence: an NE selector relocation on the slot or immediate that loads ES, resolved to the object's segment. Prefer the packet's addressed_segment and exact_mapsym_names.

The CONST selector pool is private to one object and ordered by first reference across the whole unit; a function whose pool constraints conflict in isolation needs its unit context, and functions sharing a pool word belong to the same unit.

The compiler profile belongs to the unit context (layout/compiler-profiles.json): use the packet profile as given; a code-shape mismatch that only /Og explains is profile evidence for the unit (report it), not a per-function flag to try.

Inline REP STOSW/MOVSW from simple loops and struct copies are ordinary /Oelw code; REPNE SCASB (strlen) or REP MOVSB over a computed length are /Oi intrinsic fingerprints and count as profile evidence for the unit rather than as hand-written loops.

MSC 7 compiles a dense `switch` into `cmp ax,N; ja default; shl ax,1; xchg bx,ax; jmp word ptr cs:[bx+T]` with the N+1 case offsets stored as `dw` rows right after the jump (the packet shows them as `dw offset X`; the cases are `sub`-normalised so `sub ax,5; cmp ax,8` means cases 5..13 with holes pointing at `default`). Write a plain `switch` on the value with exactly those case labels; holes are absent cases, shared targets are fall-through or identical labels, `default:` only when the ja target does real work. Case body order follows the source order; `break` tails become `jmp` to the common exit and each body except the last is followed by an alignment `nop`. Sparse switches compile to compare chains instead; do not force a table.
